title: JANUS UAP / POSS-I — Non-Nuclear Baseline + Trigger/Modulator Corrective Audit
purpose: Continue the JANUS UAP registry by separating nuclear fireball optical phenomenology from POSS-I photographic transients, documenting transient candidates observed outside nuclear-test windows, auditing older UAP registry claims against current open sources, and replacing a generator-only nuclear hypothesis with a falsifiable baseline-plus-trigger/modulator model.

epistemic_labels.FACT: Directly documented by a suitable source or reproducible measurement.
epistemic_labels.REPORTED_RESULT: A published statistical or observational result that has not yet passed JANUS independent reproduction.
epistemic_labels.CONTESTED_RESULT: A reported result with a material published methodological challenge or incompatible replication/reanalysis.
epistemic_labels.INTERPRETATION: A model that may explain facts but is not itself an observation.
epistemic_labels.OPEN_HYPOTHESIS: A falsifiable proposition requiring new tests.
epistemic_labels.SPECULATIVE_MODEL: A testable but currently weakly evidenced explanatory model; no evidential promotion is allowed from novelty alone.

NUCLEAR_FIREBALL_DOUBLE_PULSE.definition: Atmospheric nuclear detonations can show two characteristic optical light pulses as the shock-heated opaque air initially suppresses visible emission and later becomes transparent while cooling.
NUCLEAR_FIREBALL_DOUBLE_PULSE.measurement_requirement: high-time-resolution optical photometry or high-speed film/video
NUCLEAR_FIREBALL_DOUBLE_PULSE.source: Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory, declassified nuclear-test film reanalysis

POSS1_STARLIKE_TRANSIENT.definition: A point-like feature found in digitized POSS-I photographic material, present on one exposure and absent on temporally adjacent or later survey images under the dataset's selection rules.
POSS1_STARLIKE_TRANSIENT.timescale_constraint: less than one photographic exposure; commonly <= 50 minutes, not millisecond-resolved
POSS1_STARLIKE_TRANSIENT.critical_boundary: A POSS-I point source does not preserve the millisecond-to-second nuclear double-pulse light curve. Therefore nuclear double-pulse phenomenology and POSS-I transients must never be treated as the same observable merely because both are described as flashes.

UAP_REPORT.definition: A report or sensor observation that was unidentified at a stated analysis stage. Unidentified does not imply anomalous performance, non-human origin, extraterrestrial origin, or a common physical class across reports.

uap_binary_test.important_context: At least one UFOCAT report existed on 89.3% of dates, making a binary UAP/no-UAP exposure poorly discriminating.

uap_count_test.reported_interpretation: Each additional independent UAP report was associated with an 8.5% increase in transient count in the fitted model.

core_open_source_result.janus_interpretation: The published data themselves demonstrate a non-zero transient baseline outside nuclear-test windows. Therefore a nuclear test cannot be a necessary condition for this catalogued phenomenon. At most, the reported result proposes an excess/modulation around test windows, and that excess is presently contested by later reanalysis.

documented_non_nuclear_or_non_test_conte.description: Nine point-like sources appeared in a small field on a POSS-I red plate and were absent in nearby-in-time and modern images.
documented_non_nuclear_or_non_test_conte.nuclear_context: No nuclear-test trigger is required to define this event; it predates the 1951-1957 above-ground test sequence emphasized in the 2025 nuclear-correlation study. Final window membership must still be mechanically verified against the frozen test-date table before quantitative admission.

critical_source.citation: Hambly & Blair, RAS Techniques and Instruments 3, 73-79 (2024)
critical_source.claim: The putative transients are likely spurious emulsion/copying artefacts based on morphology/classification of the copy-plate material.

response_source.claim: Short sub-second optical flashes can appear sharper and rounder than stars in a long photographic exposure, so morphology alone may not uniquely identify emulsion defects.

documented_non_nuclear_or_non_test_conte.description: Three approximately 16th-magnitude point sources within about 10 arcsec vanished within less than one hour and remained absent in deep follow-up observations over decades.
documented_non_nuclear_or_non_test_conte.nuclear_context: The 2025 Scientific Reports paper introduces the July 19 and July 27 examples specifically while discussing UAP associations outside the nuclear-testing context.
documented_non_nuclear_or_non_test_conte.uap_context: The dates overlap the two famous July 1952 Washington, D.C. UAP-report weekends; this is temporal context, not proof that the photographic features and UAP reports share a cause.

source.citation: Solano et al., Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society 527, 6312-6320 (2024)

documented_non_nuclear_or_non_test_conte.description: Multiple bright transients are cited by Bruehl & Villarroel as a second July 1952 example in their discussion of UAP reports outside the nuclear-testing context.
At least one transient was reported on 10.8% of dates outside the study's nuclear-test windows, compared with 15.6% inside windows.
documented_non_nuclear_or_non_test_conte.importance: This is stronger than any single anecdotal case for the logical question of necessity: the catalogued phenomenon is common enough outside the nuclear exposure definition that nuclear testing cannot be the sole generator in the published model.

contested_reanalysis_matrix.result: Reports RR=1.45 for nuclear-window transient occurrence, p=0.008, plus UAP-count associations.

Reports that the nuclear-test correlation becomes insignificant after normalization by relevant observation days and is almost completely determined by the Palomar observation schedule; also reports dataset-definition, catalogue-star, scan-artifact, plate-defect, edge/corner-density and spatial-structure concerns.
contested_reanalysis_matrix.effect_on_registry: Nuclear correlation remains CONTESTED, not CONFIRMED.

contested_reanalysis_matrix.result: Using the original dataset, reproduces RR=1.45 (p=0.011), reports negative-binomial effects after precipitation/lunar/cloud controls and a 10,000-iteration permutation p=0.006.
contested_reanalysis_matrix.effect_on_registry: Prevents dismissal of the original effect solely because one critical reanalysis disagrees; exact exposure definitions must be harmonized and reproduced side-by-side.

contested_reanalysis_matrix.result: Reports strong suppression of transient detections at high Kp and argues geomagnetic state is an additional physical covariate while the nuclear coefficient survives in that model.
contested_reanalysis_matrix.effect_on_registry: Kp/Ap and solar/geomagnetic conditions become mandatory covariates; the physical interpretation is not admitted from this preprint alone.

legacy_registry_corrections.old_problem: The legacy entry treats the +68% result as a high-confidence VASCO fact and assigns strong confidence before the 2025 publication and 2026 methodological dispute were available.
legacy_registry_corrections.replacement: Version as Bruehl & Villarroel 2025 REPORTED_RESULT with nuclear association CONTESTED; +68% refers specifically to the one-day-after-test comparison, while the preregistered/primary +/-1-day window RR was +45%.

legacy_registry_corrections.old_problem: Marked confirmed / peer-reviewed with point-estimate confidence 0.96 and used as a high-weight Bayesian input.
legacy_registry_corrections.replacement: Preserve posterior 0.099 only as VERSIONED_HISTORICAL_OUTPUT. Current evidence label is CONTESTED_UNTIL_EXPOSURE_NORMALIZED_REPRODUCTION. Do not convert a study p-value or publication status into a subjective probability that the nuclear-attraction hypothesis is true.

legacy_registry_corrections.old_problem: Legacy wording describes 144 objects as unexplained anomalies with very high confidence.
legacy_registry_corrections.replacement: The Galileo commissioning paper reconstructed approximately 500,000 trajectories over five months; a toy sinuosity search flagged about 16%, and manual review left 144 ambiguous trajectories that the authors state are likely mundane but cannot yet be elucidated without distance/kinematics or additional sensors. Ambiguous is not equivalent to anomalous UAP.

legacy_registry_corrections.target: data/janus-meta-registry-v10.0-uap-meta.json::AARO_2024 and generic registry use of unresolved
legacy_registry_corrections.old_problem: Legacy summaries risk treating unresolved cases as anomalous cases.
legacy_registry_corrections.replacement: AARO explicitly distinguishes unresolved because of insufficient data from cases with anomalous characteristics. Current AARO closed-case outcomes through 2026 are dominated by balloons and satellites; unresolved must not be upgraded to extraordinary behavior without performance evidence.
legacy_registry_corrections.current_note: AARO lists an FY2025 consolidated annual report as released on 2026-07-20; claims should be refreshed from that report before carrying forward old FY2024 percentages.

legacy_registry_corrections.old_problem: Phrases such as 'maneuvered beyond known physics' or 'verified_by_military=true' can collapse witness/sensor provenance into verification of extraordinary performance.
legacy_registry_corrections.replacement: Split every incident into OBSERVATION_VERIFIED, IDENTITY_RESOLVED, KINEMATICS_VALIDATED, ANOMALOUS_PERFORMANCE_VALIDATED and ORIGIN_VALIDATED fields. Military provenance verifies that a report/sensor record exists; it does not automatically validate every interpretation of the event.

new_baseline_plus_trigger_model.core_statement: Assume a non-zero baseline rate of candidate transient features. Nuclear testing, geomagnetic state, atmospheric ionization, observation conditions, reporting intensity, or other variables may modulate the detection/event rate. The analysis must estimate modifiers rather than assume nuclear events generate the entire phenomenon.
new_baseline_plus_trigger_model.rate_equation: lambda_i = exposure_i * lambda0 * exp(beta_nuclear*N_i + beta_uap*U_i + beta_Kp*Kp_i + beta_weather*W_i + beta_lunar*L_i + beta_plate*P_i + beta_schedule*S_i + beta_site*X_i)

terms.exposure_i: actual usable plate area / observation opportunity / time
terms.N_i: nuclear-test predictor; test day, lag windows, yield, distance and geometry should be tested separately
terms.U_i: UAP-report count or independently quality-weighted UAP variable
terms.Kp_i: geomagnetic state; Kp/Ap and, where possible, solar-wind/auroral indices
terms.W_i: weather / cloud / transparency / precipitation / lightning context
terms.P_i: plate identity, emulsion/copy lineage, scanner, edge distance, defects and quality metrics
terms.S_i: Palomar schedule / date / season / telescope-use structure
terms.X_i: field/site/sky-position terms and other preregistered covariates

new_baseline_plus_trigger_model.primary_question: After exposure, schedule, plate-quality and geomagnetic controls, is beta_nuclear distinguishable from zero and stable to reasonable window definitions?
new_baseline_plus_trigger_model.secondary_question: Do verified non-nuclear cases share morphology, spatial distribution, solar geometry or geomagnetic conditions with nuclear-window cases?
new_baseline_plus_trigger_model.interpretive_ceiling: A surviving beta_nuclear supports an association with nuclear context. It does not establish that UAP are attracted to nuclear weapons, that the transients are physical objects, or that any non-human agency exists.

competing_hypotheses.label: NULL / ARTIFACT
competing_hypotheses.description: Most or all candidate transients arise from photographic emulsion, copy-plate processes, scanning, catalogue mismatch, plate-position systematics and observation-schedule confounding.
predictions: Effects weaken or disappear on original plate material or independent rescans.
Candidate density tracks plate edges/corners, copy lineage, scanner or plate-quality metrics.
Nuclear coefficients collapse after correct exposure/schedule normalization.

competing_hypotheses.label: OPEN_HYPOTHESIS
competing_hypotheses.description: A subset are genuine short optical sky events, potentially heterogeneous, with ordinary or unusual astrophysical/atmospheric causes.
predictions: Independent original-plate scans preserve the same sky-coordinate PSF features.
Events show physically coherent wavelength, PSF and spatial distributions inconsistent with emulsion defects.
Modern high-cadence surveys identify a matching population after selection-function correction.

competing_hypotheses.label: OPEN_HYPOTHESIS
competing_hypotheses.description: Some features are short solar glints from high-altitude or near-Earth reflecting objects.
predictions: Strong dependence on Sun-object-observer geometry and Earth's shadow.
Possible aligned/multiple flashes for rotating or grouped reflectors.
Modern multi-station parallax or synchronized optical observations should constrain distance.

competing_hypotheses.label: OPEN_HYPOTHESIS
competing_hypotheses.description: Nuclear tests do not generate all transients but may perturb atmospheric/ionospheric conditions and temporarily change the rate or visibility of a pre-existing class.
predictions: Non-zero baseline outside test windows remains.
Any nuclear effect scales more coherently with yield, altitude, distance, ionization/fallout geometry or lag than with a simple binary test-date flag.
Comparable non-nuclear ionization disturbances may create similar modulation.

competing_hypotheses.label: OPEN_HYPOTHESIS
competing_hypotheses.description: The relevant modifier may be broader magnetospheric/ionospheric state rather than nuclear testing itself; nuclear events would then be one possible perturbation among several.
predictions: Rate depends reproducibly on Kp/Ap, solar-wind, auroral or lightning/ionization variables in independent datasets.
A model trained without nuclear labels predicts some of the apparent nuclear-window excess.
Non-nuclear events cluster in the same physical-state region as nuclear-window events.

competing_hypotheses.label: OPEN_HYPOTHESIS
competing_hypotheses.description: A subset of validated optical transients and a subset of independently validated UAP reports may arise from a common object population or common environmental driver.
predictions: Association survives reporting-bias correction and quality weighting.
Time/location/geometry relationships are stronger for sensor-verified UAP than for unvetted witness reports.
Independent modern multi-sensor observations produce simultaneous optical and kinematic evidence.
competing_hypotheses.forbidden_upgrade: No extraterrestrial or non-human origin may be inferred from correlation alone.

competing_hypotheses.label: SPECULATIVE_MODEL
competing_hypotheses.description: A 2026 preprint by Ariel Zhitnitsky proposes axion quark nuggets (AQNs) as a common explanation for POSS-I mysterious transients, nuclear-test timing, alignments and UAP/ball-lightning-like phenomena.
competing_hypotheses.reason_for_zero_current_weight: New single-author preprint; the model is not an independently established explanation of the POSS-I features. It is retained only because it proposes concrete tests and naturally motivates comparison of nuclear and non-nuclear ionization triggers.
competing_hypotheses.admission_rule: May gain weight only through preregistered predictions that outperform H0-H5 on independent data without post-hoc parameter tuning.

required_controls: Freeze exact transient catalogue version and every plate/copy/scanner provenance field.
Freeze exact nuclear-test table and define test-day, +/-1 day and lag windows before fitting.
Use actual observation opportunity / plate exposure as offset; do not use calendar days as if every day had equal sky exposure.
Analyze original plate material or the closest available independent scans where possible; distinguish original negatives from copy plates.
Model plate-edge distance, local defects, emulsion/copy batch and scanner provenance.
Use pseudo-event nuclear dates preserving season and observation schedule.
Include Kp/Ap, solar activity, lunar illumination, weather/cloud/precipitation and lightning where available.
Replace binary nuclear exposure with yield, burst altitude/type, distance from Palomar and physically motivated lag variables in secondary models.
Quality-weight UAP data; separate radar/multisensor/military records from unvetted witness-only reports.
Run the nuclear model without UAP, the UAP model without nuclear, a joint model, and a no-physical-trigger artifact/schedule model.
Hold out entire plates and date blocks for out-of-sample validation rather than random row splitting.
Require effect-direction stability under preregistered candidate-quality thresholds.
Report null results and failed replications with the same provenance depth as positive results.

decisive_comparisons.pass_condition: A validated candidate population remains outside all nuclear windows after plate-quality and exposure controls.
decisive_comparisons.meaning: Rejects any model in which nuclear tests are a necessary generator of the entire phenomenon.

decisive_comparisons.pass_condition: A preregistered nuclear coefficient survives schedule/exposure, plate-quality, geomagnetic, weather and pseudo-date controls with stable direction and useful effect size.
decisive_comparisons.meaning: Supports nuclear context as a rate modifier only.

decisive_comparisons.pass_condition: Nuclear-window and non-nuclear validated events occupy a shared independently measured physical-state region (e.g. geomagnetic/ionization variables) that predicts events out of sample.
decisive_comparisons.meaning: Supports a broader trigger family and may demote the binary nuclear label from causal candidate to proxy variable.

decisive_comparisons.pass_condition: Effects disappear on original/independent scans or after plate/schedule controls.
decisive_comparisons.meaning: Rejects a physical nuclear/UAP interpretation for the affected dataset even if the original calendar correlation was statistically significant.

modern_observation_design.goal: Search for a modern analogue without relying on historical witness labels.
minimum_sensor_stack: high-frame-rate visible photometry capable of resolving sub-second pulse structure
two or more separated stations for parallax
GNSS TEC / ionospheric context where available
geomagnetic Kp/Ap and local magnetometer data
modern_observation_design.key_discriminator: A true nuclear fireball double pulse, a sub-second reflected glint, a lightning-related optical event, an aircraft/satellite, and a persistent astronomical source produce different time profiles, parallax, spectra and motion. Modern instrumentation should classify these observables before any UAP label is applied.

AARO.closed_case_pattern: AARO's current closed-case table is dominated by balloons and satellites, with smaller UAS/aircraft/bird and other categories.
AARO.interpretation: This does not prove all UAP are mundane; it demonstrates that resolution of many cases is prosaic and that an unresolved label cannot be used as a proxy for extraordinary performance.

GALILEO_PROJECT.correct_reading: Approximately 500,000 reconstructed trajectories over five months; toy sinuosity outlier search flags ~16%; 144 remain ambiguous after manual review and are described by the authors as likely mundane but not elucidated with the commissioning sensor stack.
GALILEO_PROJECT.registry_rule: Do not call the 144 confirmed anomalous UAP.

registry_level_conclusion.highest_value_next_data: original/copy-plate provenance + observation exposure + independently rescanned plate pixels + physically measured geomagnetic/ionization covariates

fail_closed_rules: A nuclear double flash != a POSS-I point-source candidate.
A p-value != probability that a favored ontology is true.
A preprint supporting a preferred hypothesis cannot outrank a conflicting methodological critique without reproduction.
A military or government source can verify provenance of a report without validating every claimed kinematic interpretation.
Any new model must explain the non-nuclear baseline, not only nuclear-window excesses.
The artifact/schedule null remains active until original-plate or equivalent provenance controls pass.

next_action.action: Freeze and retrieve the exact 107,875-feature transient catalogue, plate IDs/exposure schedule, copy/scanner provenance and exact nuclear-test table, then create a plate-day exposure matrix before fitting any new nuclear/UAP/geomagnetic model.
